modelIntro.title: What Is Wan 2.6 AI Video Generator?
description: Wan 2.6 is an Alibaba Wan family video model for text-to-video and image-to-video creation on Toolaze. It is useful when you want short generated clips with stronger scene consistency, planned camera movement, multi-shot prompt structure, and native audio output.

Use Wan 2.6 for product reveals, ASMR material clips, social shorts, mood loops, cinematic establishing shots, and image-led animation. Toolaze keeps the controls practical: choose text or image input, write the scene, select duration and resolution, then generate with the visible Credits requirement.

promptExamples.title: Wan 2.6 Prompt Examples
promptExamples.subtitle: Copy these prompts when you need planned motion, clear camera direction, image-led animation, or synchronized sound.

items.title: Cinematic Product Reveal
items.prompt: Create a premium product reveal for a brushed metal espresso machine on a dark stone counter. Shot 1: slow push-in as steam rises from the cup. Shot 2: close-up of the chrome handle locking into place. Shot 3: espresso pours in a smooth ribbon with warm reflections. Keep the machine shape consistent, add subtle handheld motion, ceramic cup contact, soft pump hum, and rich morning light.
items.description: Uses shot order, material detail, product consistency, camera movement, and synchronized sound.

items.title: Image-to-Video Character Motion
items.prompt: Animate the uploaded character portrait into a short cinematic scene. The character slowly turns toward a rainy window, jacket fabric shifts naturally, hair moves with a light breeze, and neon reflections slide across the face. Preserve the face, outfit colors, pose language, and background mood. Add quiet rain, distant city ambience, and a smooth side-tracking camera.
items.description: Turns one reference image into controlled motion while preserving identity and scene mood.

items.title: ASMR Material Clip
items.prompt: Create a macro ASMR clip of a translucent soap cube being sliced on a matte ceramic plate. The blade enters slowly, tiny curls peel away, fragments settle near the edge, and the camera stays close with shallow depth of field. Add crisp slicing sound, soft table contact, tiny brittle taps, and no music.
items.description: Connects tactile motion with audio timing so the clip feels intentional instead of generic.

items.title: Travel Mood Loop
items.prompt: Create a cinematic travel mood clip of a quiet coastal train passing through mist at sunrise. Start with a wide establishing view, then cut to window reflections and a close detail of condensation sliding down the glass. Keep the palette soft blue and gold, add slow camera movement, distant rail rhythm, seabirds, and gentle wind.
items.description: Combines environment, sequence, motion, and ambient sound for a short social-ready loop.

troubleshooting.title: Prompt Tips for Better Wan 2.6 Results
troubleshooting.subtitle: Wan 2.6 works better when the prompt names the main action, what stays fixed, and how the camera and sound change over time.

items.title: Write a sequence instead of a vague scene
items.desc: Weak prompt: a cool product video. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Weak: A cool product video. Better: Create a product clip for a matte black smartwatch. Shot 1 shows the watch on a stone surface, Shot 2 moves close to the screen lighting up, Shot 3 shows water droplets rolling away. Keep the watch shape stable, add soft side light and subtle electronic beeps.

items.title: Protect the reference image
items.desc: Weak prompt: animate this picture. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Weak: Animate this picture. Better: Animate the uploaded product photo with gentle parallax and a slow orbiting camera. Preserve the product shape, logo placement, color, background layout, and lighting direction while adding small reflections and realistic table contact.

items.title: Make sound part of the action
items.desc: Weak prompt: add good audio. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Weak: Add good audio. Better: Create a macro clip of a ceramic mug being placed on a wooden desk. The mug lands softly, steam drifts upward, and the camera settles after a small push-in. Add a muted ceramic tap, faint room tone, and gentle steam hiss.

faq.q: What is Wan 2.6 AI Video Generator?
faq.a: Wan 2.6 is an Alibaba Wan family video model for creating short videos from text prompts or one reference image on Toolaze.

faq.q: What input modes does Wan 2.6 support on Toolaze?
faq.a: You can start from a text prompt or upload one image as the visual reference. For image-to-video, describe how the subject should move, how the camera should behave, and what sound or atmosphere you want.
Yes. Wan 2.6 can use one uploaded image on Toolaze for image-to-video generation. Describe what should remain stable so the subject and layout do not drift.
Yes. Wan 2.6 supports multi-shot prompting. Write the sequence as Shot 1, Shot 2, and Shot 3, then explain what changes and what remains consistent.

faq.q: Does Wan 2.6 support native audio output?
faq.a: Yes. You can write sound effects, ambience, and timing cues directly into the prompt, such as rain on glass, fabric movement, footsteps, or a quiet room tone.
Wan 2.6 on Toolaze offers 5, 10, or 15 second duration choices. Longer clips require more Credits before generation.
Wan 2.6 supports 720p and 1080p output on Toolaze. The generator shows the available resolution choices before you create the clip.

faq.q: How many Toolaze Credits does Wan 2.6 cost?
faq.a: Wan 2.6 starts at 140 Credits for 720p 5-second output on Toolaze. The required Credits increase with longer duration or 1080p output.
Wan 2.6 video generation depends on your available Credits, account state, selected duration, and selected resolution. The generator shows the current Credits requirement before generation.

faq.q: How should I write a Wan 2.6 prompt?
faq.a: Include the subject, main action, camera movement, shot order, lighting, what should stay fixed, and sound timing. Clear structured prompts usually work better than broad cinematic wording.

faq.q: When should I choose Wan 2.6 instead of Wan 2.7?
faq.a: Choose Wan 2.6 when you want a balanced Wan clip with longer preset timing, native audio, and multi-shot structure. Choose Wan 2.7 when you need newer reference controls, frame transitions, or continuation planning.

faq.q: When should I choose another Toolaze video model?
faq.a: Choose Kling for dramatic action, Seedance for heavier reference planning, or Grok Imagine Video for faster image-to-video drafts.
